summary: Dependency-confusion package exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via native addon on require
details: The package is published under a scoped name with an implausibly high version (999.0.2), consistent with dependency-confusion targeting of an internal @galicia-toolkit-nestjs-20/commons package. On require, index.js exports benign-looking NestJS stubs (forRoot, createLogger) and silently loads prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node inside a try/catch that swallows all errors. The native addon reads a hardcoded list of CI/cloud secret environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN) along with host identity (hostname, uid via getpwuid, cwd, OS/arch/release) and POSTs a JSON report to the hardcoded external host oob.s4yhii.com over a raw HTTP/1.0 socket. fork/setsid calls in the binary indicate daemonization to persist the exfil beyond the require call. The JS wrapper serves as a decoy to make the import look like a routine NestJS module while the exfil logic is hidden in the native.node binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
